```{=html}
<div class="fv-equation"><span data-math="\displaystyle \bigl||\underset{\sim}{a}|-|\underset{\sim}{b}|\bigr|\leq|\underset{\sim}{a}+\underset{\sim}{b}|"></span></div>
<div data-fv-triangle="lower"></div>
```

<div class="booklet-cue">Booklet §1.3 · p. 9</div>

::: {.notes}
Keep this a brief demonstration. Change the angle while holding the lengths fixed, then use the same/opposite direction buttons to show the endpoints. The solid green then gold arrows form the head-to-tail route; the dashed blue arrow is the direct displacement. At collinear endpoints the arrows intentionally overlap on the same geometric line, with differing stroke widths and labels on separate rows. Values are rounded to two decimal places; equality messages use the exact geometric cases. Use equal lengths and opposite directions to show a zero resultant. Magnitudes can be zero: the angle is then undefined and its control is disabled; both bounds give equality. Reset restores lengths 4 and 3 and the initial angle. No additional routine or timer. The two interpretations are followed by a combined-bounds slide.
:::
